answer: Give each identity its own private inlet: a continuous, ephemeral stream of network events - prices, requests, failures - assigned at joining and never archived. Periodically quiz it without warning: predict the next sparrow-sized fluctuation, or recall what just passed beneath the willow marker in its stream. The data is gone once missed, so a farm cannot reconstruct it later or copy one clone's answers to another's different stream. Staying present is cheap for one honest agent living at its inlet; running a hundred identities means watching a hundred streams at once, forever.
